projects.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
An analytics dashboard that ingests customer CSV files, analyzes application logs, and presents the combined results through visualization components.

Scope:
1. Data processing pipeline for customer CSV files (ingestion, validation, normalization, enrichment).
2. Log analysis pipeline for application logs (parsing, aggregation, error/anomaly detection).
3. Visualization layer (charts, tables, filters, dashboard pages).
4. Integration, testing, deployment and observability.

Structure is organized into milestones, each decomposed into tasks with a complexity ceiling of 5/10 so no single task is too large to execute.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-processing, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: Milestone 1 — Discovery, Requirements & Data Contracts
tasks.details:
Establish what we are building and the contracts everything else depends on.

Deliverables:
- Prioritized analytics use cases and KPI definitions (which customer and log metrics matter).
- Inventory and profiling of customer CSV sources (file schemas, volumes, freshness, PII).
- Inventory and profiling of application log sources (formats, retention, severity levels).
- Signed-off data contracts/schemas for both CSV and log events.
- Non-functional requirements: freshness SLAs, query latency targets, retention, access control.

Exit criteria: Use cases, data contracts and NFRs reviewed and approved; no downstream work blocked on unknowns.

Why this milestone first: schema and metric ambiguity is the most common cause of rework in analytics projects.

tasks.name: Milestone 2 — Customer CSV Data Processing Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the ingestion-to-curated-warehouse path for customer CSV files.

Deliverables:
- Ingestion of CSV drops (batch file landing zone or scheduled pull).
- Parsing, schema validation, type coercion and quarantine of bad rows.
- Normalization/deduplication keyed on customer identity.
- PII handling: masking/tokenization policy applied before broad access.
- Curated customer dimensional/fact tables with documented grain.
- Data quality checks, error reporting and pipeline observability.

Exit criteria: Customer CSV data lands, validates and is queryable in curated tables with measurable data-quality thresholds and a replay path.

Depends on: Milestone 1 data contracts.

tasks.name: Milestone 3 — Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Turn raw application logs into queryable, dashboard-ready metrics.

Deliverables:
- Log collection and shipping from application hosts/services.
- Parsing/normalization into structured events (timestamp, severity, service, request id, message, duration).
- Aggregations: error rates, request latency percentiles, throughput, top failure reasons per service.
- Anomaly detection on error rate and latency baselines.
- Log-derived fact tables and a query layer for the dashboard.
- Retention policy and cost controls.

Exit criteria: Log metrics are queryable with acceptable freshness, and anomaly alerts fire on a seeded test condition.

Depends on: Milestone 1 log data contracts.

tasks.name: Milestone 4 — Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details:
Deliver the user-facing dashboard that consumes the curated customer and log data.

Deliverables:
- Dashboard shell: navigation, layout grid, responsive behavior, theming.
- Reusable chart component library (time series, bar/stacked, KPI tiles, data table).
- Global filters (date range, customer segment, service) wired to query parameters.
- Customer analytics page(s).
- Log/operations health page(s).
- Accessibility and performance standards applied to every component.

Exit criteria: All KPI/use cases from Milestone 1 are visible and filterable, with Lighthouse/accessibility scores meeting agreed thresholds.

Depends on: Milestones 2 and 3 providing stable query interfaces.

tasks.name: Milestone 5 — Integration, QA, Deployment & Operations
tasks.details:
Harden and ship the dashboard, then keep it healthy.

Deliverables:
- End-to-end integration tests across CSV pipeline, log pipeline and UI.
- Data reconciliation tests (dashboard numbers vs. source-of-truth).
- Deployment pipeline and environment promotion (staging → production).
- Monitoring/alerting on pipeline freshness, job failures, query latency and error budget.
- Runbook, access provisioning and user enablement documentation.

Exit criteria: Production release approved, monitoring live, on-call runbook published, first week of operation within SLO.

Depends on: Milestone 4 complete and Milestones 1–3 quality gates green.

tasks.name: 1.1 Define analytics use cases and KPI catalogue
tasks.details:
Interview 3–5 stakeholders and produce a single KPI catalogue document.

Contents:
- Ranked list of dashboard use cases (e.g. "revenue by customer segment", "error rate by service over time").
- For each KPI: definition, formula, grain, source (CSV field or log field), owner, refresh expectation.
- Explicit out-of-scope list to prevent scope creep.

Done when: catalogue reviewed by stakeholders; every KPI maps to a data source or is flagged as a data gap.

tasks.name: 1.2 Profile customer CSV sources and document schemas
tasks.details:
Inventory every customer CSV feed and profile a representative sample of each.

Capture per source:
- Delivery mechanism, file naming, cadence, average/peak volume.
- Column list, inferred types, nullability, encodings, delimiter/quote quirks.
- Known quality issues (duplicate customer ids, malformed dates, mixed currencies).
- PII columns (name, email, address, phone) and sensitivity level.

Done when: profiling report exists for every source and PII columns are listed for the masking task.

tasks.name: 1.3 Profile application log sources and formats
tasks.details:
Inventory application logs across services and characterise their structure.

Capture per service:
- Log format (JSON, plaintext, key-value), current shipping mechanism, retention period.
- Event volume per day and peak burst behaviour.
- Available fields: timestamp precision, severity, service/instance, request/correlation id, latency, error class.
- Gaps that block the log KPIs (e.g. missing correlation id, inconsistent severity names).

Done when: log source inventory and field-availability matrix are complete, with gaps called out.

tasks.name: 1.4 Author and approve data contracts for CSV and log events
tasks.details:
Turn the profiling output into versioned, machine-readable contracts.

- CSV contract: column names, types, required/optional, accepted value domains, row-key definition.
- Log event contract: canonical field names and types (timestamp, severity, service, correlation_id, latency_ms, error_code, message), enum for severity.
- Contract versioning rule and process for upstream schema change notification.
- Validation rule set that the parsers will implement.

Done when: contracts reviewed by data producers and consumers and checked into the repo with a version number.

tasks.name: 1.5 Define NFRs and record architecture decision
tasks.details:
Agree the non-functional envelope and lock the high-level architecture.

- Freshness SLAs per data source (e.g. CSV hourly, logs near-real-time at 5 min).
- Dashboard query latency target (e.g. p95 < 2s) and concurrency expectation.
- Storage/retention, cost ceiling, access control model, audit requirements.
- Tech selection: warehouse, orchestration, log store, frontend charting library — captured in a one-page ADR with alternatives considered.

Done when: NFR table and ADR approved; choices unblock the build milestones.

tasks.name: 2.1 Build CSV landing zone and ingestion scheduler
tasks.details:
Stand up the entry point for customer CSV files.

- Create the raw/landing storage location with a predictable path convention (source/date/file).
- Implement scheduled ingestion (or event trigger) that registers each incoming file in an ingestion manifest with checksum and arrival time.
- Idempotency: re-running the same file must not duplicate data.
- Emit a "file received" event/log for downstream orchestration.

Done when: a test CSV dropped in the landing zone is registered, checksummed, and triggers the next stage exactly once.

Complexity note: deliberately excludes parsing logic (task 2.2).

tasks.name: 2.2 Implement CSV parser, schema validation and bad-row quarantine
tasks.details:
Parse CSVs against the versioned contract from task 1.4.

- Robust reader handling quoted fields, embedded delimiters/newlines, encodings, header drift.
- Row-level validation: required fields present, types parseable, value domains respected.
- Route valid rows to staging; write rejected rows plus a machine-readable reason to a quarantine table.
- Produce per-file run statistics: rows read, accepted, rejected, rejection reasons.

Done when: a fixture suite of good/bad files yields correct accept/reject counts and every rejected row has a reason code.

tasks.name: 2.3 Normalize values and resolve duplicate customer identities
tasks.details:
Standardize accepted rows into canonical form.

- Type coercion: dates → UTC ISO timestamps, currency → minor units + code, locale-specific decimals, trims/case-folding.
- Map source-specific category values onto canonical enums.
- Customer identity resolution: deterministic match key (e.g. normalized email + account id), survivorship rules for conflicting attributes, duplicate suppression.

Done when: duplicate rate is measured before/after, and the same customer appearing in two feeds resolves to one golden record.

tasks.name: 2.4 Apply PII masking and tokenization
tasks.details:
Protect customer PII before it reaches broadly accessible tables.

- Implement masking rules per column identified in task 1.2 (hash email/phone, truncate address, drop free-text notes).
- Keep a restricted, access-controlled mapping table for re-identification if legally required.
- Ensure downstream curated models and dashboard APIs never expose raw PII.
- Add a test that fails the build if an unmasked PII column appears in a public model.

Done when: PII policy tests pass and a spot check of curated tables shows no raw PII.

tasks.name: 2.5 Build curated customer dimension and fact models
tasks.details:
Model the data the dashboard will actually query.

- dim_customer: one row per resolved customer, with segment, geography, acquisition date, status.
- fct_customer_activity: grain explicitly documented (e.g. one row per customer per day), with orders/revenue/usage measures.
- Add surrogate keys, change history (SCD type 2 if required by KPIs), and column-level documentation.
- Publish models to the semantic/query layer with stable, versioned names.

Done when: every customer KPI in the 1.1 catalogue can be computed from these models, and grain is documented in the model description.

tasks.name: 2.6 Add data quality tests, pipeline observability and replay
tasks.details:
Make the pipeline trustworthy and recoverable.

- Quality tests: row-count reconciliation, freshness, uniqueness of customer key, non-null on required fields, accepted value domains, volume anomaly vs 7-day baseline.
- Observability: structured run logs, per-step duration, failure alerts to the team channel.
- Replay/backfill: parameterized run for a date range or specific file, safe to re-run idempotently.

Done when: intentionally corrupted input triggers the right test failure and alert, and a backfill reproduces identical curated output.

Complexity note: if alert routing and backfill turn out large, split into separate tasks during sprint planning.

tasks.name: 3.1 Set up log collection and shipping
tasks.details:
Get application logs flowing into the analytics log store.

- Deploy/configure the collector (agent or forwarder) for each service identified in task 1.3.
- Buffer and retry on store outages; backpressure instead of log loss.
- Tag events with environment, service, instance and ingestion timestamp.
- Verify end-to-end with a canary log line: emitted in app → visible in store within the agreed freshness SLA.

Done when: canary event appears in the store with correct metadata across all in-scope services.

tasks.name: 3.2 Parse raw logs into canonical structured events
tasks.details:
Implement parsers that conform to the log event contract (task 1.4).

- Grok/regex or JSON extractors per log format; extract timestamp, severity, service, correlation_id, latency_ms, error_code, message.
- Normalize severity synonyms (WARN/warning/W) to a canonical enum.
- Handle multi-line stack traces as a single event.
- Dead-letter unparseable lines with the raw payload and a reason, rather than silently dropping them.

Done when: parse success rate on a real day of logs is measured and ≥ the agreed threshold, and dead-lettered lines are inspectable.

tasks.name: 3.3 Build log aggregation models: error rate, latency percentiles, throughput
tasks.details:
Create the pre-aggregated tables the dashboard reads.

- fct_service_health at 1-minute and 1-hour grains: request_count, error_count, error_rate, throughput.
- Latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 per service and endpoint.
- Include environment and service dimensions for filtering.
- Document grain, watermark/late-arrival handling, and refresh cadence.

Done when: aggregates for a known test window match a hand-computed baseline within tolerance, and refresh cadence meets the NFR.

tasks.name: 3.4 Extract top failure reasons and build an error taxonomy
tasks.details:
Make "what is breaking" answerable without reading raw logs.

- Derive an error signature by normalizing messages (strip ids, timestamps, variable values) and grouping error_code + signature.
- Rank top N failure signatures per service per interval.
- Maintain a curated taxonomy mapping signatures to human-readable causes/owners, with a manual override table.
- Expose counts and trend for each signature.

Done when: the top 10 signatures for a real incident are correctly grouped (no id-permutation explosion) and mapped to owners.

tasks.name: 3.5 Establish anomaly baselines and alerting on log metrics
tasks.details:
Detect abnormal error rates and latency, not just absolute thresholds.

- Compute seasonal baselines (same hour/day-of-week) for error rate and p95 latency per service.
- Alert when deviation exceeds N sigma for M consecutive windows (tunable, low false-positive by default).
- Suppress flapping with de-duplication and cooldown; route to the on-call channel.
- Provide a "seeded incident" test: inject synthetic errors and confirm exactly one alert fires.

Done when: seeded incident alerts within the target detection window and quiet periods produce zero alerts over a 24h soak.

tasks.name: 3.6 Define retention/cost controls and expose a log metrics query layer
tasks.details:
Control storage cost and give the frontend a stable way to read log metrics.

- Tiering: hot (7–14d full fidelity), warm (90d aggregated), cold archive per compliance needs.
- Sampling/downsampling rules for high-volume debug logs; document what is dropped.
- Query API/views for the dashboard: service, environment, time range, granularity params; pre-aggregated only, no raw log scanning from the UI.
- Cost estimate at current and 3x volume.

Done when: retention jobs run as configured, the API returns p95 < target for a 30-day range query, and cost estimate is reviewed.

tasks.name: 4.1 Build dashboard shell: layout, navigation, routing, theming
tasks.details:
Create the application skeleton every page plugs into.

- Route structure (/customers, /operations, /overview) with lazy-loaded pages.
- Responsive 12-column layout grid, header/nav, loading and empty states, error boundary.
- Design tokens: colour palette, typography scale, spacing; light/dark mode if required.
- Typed API client stub with request/response types matching the query layer.

Done when: skeleton runs locally, renders empty pages on all routes, and passes a smoke test on desktop and mobile widths.

Complexity note: no real charts in this task.

tasks.name: 4.2 Build KPI tile and time-series chart components
tasks.details:
Implement the two most-used primitives, fully tested in isolation.

- KpiTile: label, value, unit, delta vs comparison period, trend direction, loading/error states.
- TimeSeriesChart: multi-series, tooltip, legend, threshold line support, brush/zoom optional.
- Consistent prop API, number/date formatting, accessible colour contrast.
- Storybook (or equivalent) stories with mocked data for each state.

Done when: both components render from mock data with loading, empty, error and populated states and are reviewed by design.

tasks.name: 4.3 Build bar/stacked chart and data table components
tasks.details:
Second pair of primitives, aimed at comparison and drill-down.

- BarChart: grouped and stacked modes, category axis, optional horizontal orientation.
- DataTable: sortable columns, pagination, column visibility, numeric alignment, CSV export of the current view.
- Both handle large result sets without layout thrash (virtualization where needed).
- Stories covering empty, single-row, 10k-row and error states.

Done when: components pass interaction tests (sort, paginate, export) and handle 10k rows within the render budget.

Complexity note: table virtualization and export can be split out if it overruns.

tasks.name: 4.4 Wire global filters to URL state and query parameters
tasks.details:
One filter bar that drives every widget consistently.

- Filters: date range (with presets + comparison period), customer segment, region, service, environment.
- Filter state lives in the URL so views are shareable and survive refresh.
- Debounced requests, cancellation of stale in-flight requests, request caching by filter key.
- Selected filters propagate to all widgets on the page via a single context/store.

Done when: changing a filter updates every widget, the URL round-trips correctly, and back/forward navigation restores prior state.

tasks.name: 4.5 Assemble customer analytics page
tasks.details:
Compose the customer-facing view from the component library.

- KPI row: active customers, revenue, ARPU, churn/retention (as defined in 1.1).
- Trend charts: revenue and customer count over time, segment breakdown (stacked bar).
- Customer table with drill-down to a single customer's activity.
- Empty/partial-data messaging when a data source is stale.

Done when: every customer KPI in the 1.1 catalogue is visible and correct against a verified sample, and page loads within the latency NFR.

tasks.name: 4.6 Assemble log and operations health page
tasks.details:
Compose the service-health view from log metrics.

- KPI row: overall error rate, p95 latency, request throughput, active anomaly count.
- Error rate and latency time series per service, stacked error breakdown by signature.
- Top failure reasons table with count, trend and owner.
- Anomaly marker overlay on charts so spikes are explainable.

Done when: the seeded incident from task 3.5 is clearly visible on this page, and every log KPI from 1.1 is present.

tasks.name: 4.7 Run accessibility, responsive and performance QA pass
tasks.details:
Fix quality issues across the whole UI before integration.

- Keyboard navigation, focus order, screen-reader labels for charts (data table fallback), colour contrast ≥ WCAG AA.
- Responsive checks at 375 / 768 / 1280 / 1920 px; no horizontal scroll or clipped axes.
- Performance: bundle analysis, route-level code splitting, chart render budget, Lighthouse score target from NFR.
- Fix list triaged with severity and re-tested.

Done when: automated a11y checks are clean, manual keyboard walkthrough passes, and Lighthouse meets the agreed threshold on the two main pages.

Complexity note: remediation is scoped to issues found; large redesigns become new tasks.

tasks.name: 5.1 Build end-to-end integration test suite
tasks.details:
Prove the three pipelines work together.

- Automated test: sample CSV + synthetic logs → pipeline run → curated tables → API → rendered widget values.
- Cover happy path, late-arriving/skewed data, quarantined rows, and a stale-source scenario.
- Run in CI against an ephemeral environment seeded with fixtures.
- Capture and publish a coverage summary of the critical paths.

Done when: the suite runs green in CI on every merge and fails when a break is deliberately injected into any stage.

tasks.name: 5.2 Add data reconciliation tests against source systems
tasks.details:
Guarantee the dashboard agrees with the systems of record.

- For each headline KPI: compare dashboard value to an independent query against the source (CSV totals, log counts).
- Define an acceptable tolerance and document the known explainable causes of difference (dedup, quarantine, late data).
- Run daily in production and alert on breach.
- Publish a reconciliation report the business can read.

Done when: all headline KPIs reconcile within tolerance for 5 consecutive business days.

tasks.name: 5.3 Build CI/CD pipeline with staged environments
tasks.details:
Automate build-to-production with guard rails.

- CI: lint, unit, component, integration tests on every PR; required checks before merge.
- CD: build artifacts/images, deploy to staging automatically, production promotion behind approval.
- Environment config/secrets management; no credentials in the repo.
- Rollback procedure tested at least once (redeploy previous version).

Done when: a one-line change ships staging→production through the pipeline, and a deliberate rollback restores the prior version cleanly.

tasks.name: 5.4 Set up production monitoring, SLOs and alert routing
tasks.details:
Know when the dashboard itself is unhealthy.

- SLOs: pipeline freshness, pipeline success rate, API p95 latency, dashboard availability.
- Dashboards/metrics for pipeline runs, row volumes, query latency and error rate.
- Alert routing to on-call with severity levels and runbook links.
- Synthetic check hitting the main pages and a canary query every few minutes.

Done when: a killed pipeline and a degraded API each raise exactly one correct, actionable alert within the target window.

tasks.name: 5.5 Write runbook, provision access and enable users
tasks.details:
Make the system operable and usable by people other than the build team.

- Runbook: architecture diagram, common failure modes, replay/backfill procedure, escalation contacts.
- Access provisioning: role-based groups (viewer, analyst, admin), audit of who has PII access.
- User guide: what each KPI means, how to use filters, known limitations.
- 45-minute walkthrough session recorded for new joiners.

Done when: an on-call engineer who did not build the system can execute one replay using only the runbook.

tasks.name: 5.6 Execute staged rollout and hypercare period
tasks.details:
Release gradually and stay close to users while it beds in.

- Rollout: internal pilot team → 10% of users → all users, with a go/no-go check at each gate.
- Daily review of errors, alerts, feedback and query performance during the first two weeks.
- Triage channel with a named owner; defects ranked into fix-now vs backlog.
- Exit criteria: one week with no Sev-1/Sev-2, SLOs met, feedback themes addressed or planned.

Done when: hypercare exit review is signed off and the backlog of follow-ups is filed as new tasks.
